title: Oscar and the Ledger
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Hale is exhumed for a cemetery relocation and found empty, concierge Yara Villalobos — whose side work solving guests' small mysteries has made her the town's unofficial fixer — is hired by Hale's estranged granddaughter to quietly find out why. Yara discovers the body was stolen decades ago as leverage in an old crime: Hale's fortune was built on a covered-up death, and someone has been paying annual blackmail to keep it buried. As the anniversary dinner of Hale's founding approaches, Yara realizes the killer is the town archivist who has spent a lifetime curating the official record, and she traps him by feeding a falsified detail into the case file only he can access. At the anniversary toast, the trap springs; the archivist confesses to the original death and two recent murders of those who learned the truth, and Hale's fortune is redirected to the family of the man whose body once lay in that coffin.
about_author: Rafael Okafor is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who spent a decade in small coastal hotels, collecting the secrets guests leave behind at checkout. They write mysteries about people whose jobs are to notice, and whose kindness is to remember.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Keys
chapters.summary: Yara Villalobos works the concierge desk of the Marlowe Grand, solving guests' lost-ring and missing-will mysteries with quiet precision. When cemetery crews exhume town founder Edmund Hale for relocation and find the coffin empty, the whole lobby buzzes. Yara watches Police Chief Danner flounder and feels the itch of an unclosable case. Beat: competence established, hunger sparked.

chapters.title: A Granddaughter with Cold Hands
chapters.summary: Nadia Hale, the founder's estranged granddaughter, checks in under a false name and asks Yara to investigate privately — the police, she says, will only protect the family name. Yara's rule is never take a case she can't close, and something in Nadia's grief makes her break it. Beat: the hook set, a found-family thread begins.

chapters.title: What the Ground Keeps
chapters.summary: At the exhumed grave, Yara notes the coffin was opened from below with tools no gravedigger owns, and the replacement casket liner was sourced locally — someone planned this for years. The caretaker mentions an anonymous man who visits every October 14th. Beat: dread takes root; the crime is older than it looks.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Perfect Memory
chapters.summary: Yara visits town hall and meets Corwin Ashe, the archivist who maintains every Hale record with reverent precision. He is helpful, charming, and knows the case file — including a sealed coroner's detail never made public. Yara files the slip away. Beat: the antagonist introduced as an ally; reader's first chill.

chapters.title: Ledger of a Founding Family
chapters.summary: Nadia shares family letters; Yara finds a gap in 1971 — a missing month, a burned receipt, a servant named Tomás Reyes who vanishes from the payroll overnight. The founding fortune and a human disappearance share a date. Beat: inheritance theme turns sinister.

chapters.title: The Man Who Visits in October
chapters.summary: Yara stakes out the grave and finds not a blackmailer but a frightened old groundskeeper, Silas, who admits he helped rebury the coffin empty in 1972 — and that someone has paid him ever since to stay silent. Last week, he says, the payments stopped. Beat: the clock starts; fear replaces ritual.

chapters.title: A Room Nobody Booked
chapters.summary: Silas is found dead in a storage room of the Marlowe Grand — a room Yara personally checked hours earlier. Chief Danner calls it a heart attack; Yara sees the staged details and knows the killer used her hotel, her territory, as a message. Beat: guilt and fury; the case turns personal.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Read the File
chapters.summary: Yara maps everyone with access to the coroner's sealed detail: Danner, a retired deputy, the archivist, and a dead historian who died conveniently last spring. The killer isn't hiding the crime — they're curating it. Beat: the pattern emerges; the hunt narrows.

chapters.title: Nadia's Half of the Truth
chapters.summary: Nadia confesses she came to town because of anonymous letters warning her to 'ask about 1971' — letters that stopped when she arrived. Yara realizes someone wanted a Hale to dig, then wanted her silenced too. Beat: trust deepens; the found-family bond hardens into loyalty.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Wouldn't Retire Quietly
chapters.summary: Yara tracks the retired deputy to a care home; he babbles about 'the second ledger' before his nurse cuts the visit short. That night his records burn in a shed fire. The killer is erasing the paper trail faster than Yara can read it. Beat: escalating stakes; the enemy is always one step ahead.

chapters.title: What the Concierge Noticed
chapters.summary: Reviewing hotel records, Yara finds the killer's one mistake: a guest with no luggage who requested the historical archive wing's floor plan, years running, every October. The signature in the ledger book is a small, perfect hand she's seen signing visitor cards at town hall. Beat: the trap of suspicion closes on Ashe — too neatly.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: The town prepares the 150th-anniversary founding dinner; Ashe is directing the commemorative exhibit, including an empty display case labeled 'Edmund Hale, 1821–1898.' Yara realizes the killer is curating the town's memory in public, in real time. Beat: dramatic irony tightens; the deadline is now visible.

chapters.title: The Second Ledger
chapters.summary: In the archive's mislabeled boxes, Yara and Nadia find the real second ledger: payments from Hale's estate to the Reyes family, halted in 1971, and a coroner's note — Tomás Reyes died in the founding house, and Hale's coffin was his. The founder's grave has been a lie for 150 years of October dinners. Beat: the mystery's heart revealed.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: Ashe invites Yara for tea and offers her a place as 'keeper of the record' — revealing he knows exactly what she's found. He frames his murders as mercy: the town needs its founding story whole. Yara smiles and declines, heart hammering. Beat: direct confrontation masked as civility; menace fully surfaced.

chapters.title: The Detail Only He Knows
chapters.summary: Yara plants a false detail — a fabricated 1971 receipt hidden in the archive — that only someone who reads every accession would find and destroy. Two days later it's gone. Ashe has confirmed himself, and Yara has her trap, but no legal proof. Beat: the hunter becomes the architect.

chapters.title: Chief Danner's Debt
chapters.summary: Yara confronts Danner, who admits he's known about the empty coffin's implications for years and looked away — his career was built on not asking. She gives him one chance to stand on the right side of history. Beat: justice outside the law requires converting its guardians.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Toast
chapters.summary: Yara and Nadia prepare the exhibit room, swapping Ashe's curated display for the second ledger's evidence, and set the false receipt as final bait. Nadia is terrified; Yara promises her this case will close. Beat: quiet dread before the storm; the family-of-two solidifies.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: The town raises its glasses to Edmund Hale while Yara watches Ashe discover the planted receipt — and watch him leave his seat to burn it. She follows him into the archive wing as the toast begins downstairs. Beat: the trap springs; the climax ignites.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Record
chapters.summary: In the archive, Ashe confesses with terrible calm: he killed the historian and Silas to protect the town's 'single true story,' just as his father, the 1971 coroner, falsified Reyes's death before him. He moves to add Yara to the record — and Danner steps out of the stacks with handcuffs and a recording. Beat: violence averted by prepared allies; confession delivered.

chapters.title: What the Coffin Was For
chapters.summary: The full truth goes public: Hale's fortune rests on Tomás Reyes's unmarked death, and the coffin held his body as silent blackmail against the family's conscience. Yara insists the story be told with Reyes's name restored, not just Hale's exposed. Beat: justice reframed as restoration, not punishment.

chapters.title: The Reyes Ledger, Balanced
chapters.summary: The court freezes the Hale trust; Nadia, the last heir, redirects it to Reyes's surviving descendants, who arrive in town to reclaim their grandfather's name. Silas's grave finally gets visitors. Yara watches a town rewrite itself in real time. Beat: inheritance repaid; the found family widens.

chapters.title: Concierge, On Duty
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Yara returns to the desk, a new brass key tag on her ring: the archive room, where she now volunteers. A guest hesitantly asks for help finding someone. Yara smiles, opens the ledger of open questions she keeps, and says yes. Beat: resolution and renewal — the fixer closes this case and opens the next.
